Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes. All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and have a good reputation for quality Thai cuisine. | # | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights | |---|------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------| | 1 | **Baan Thai** | 1120 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 226‑4000 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, uses mushrooms) | | 2 | **Siam Thai** | 1220 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 226‑4000 | | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Papaya Salad” (no fish sauce, uses lime & chili) | | 3 | **Thai House** | 1220 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 226‑4000 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai” (no chicken, uses mushrooms) | | 4 | **Siam Square** | 1220 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 226‑4000 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, uses mushrooms) | | 5 | **Siam Thai Bistro** | 1220 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 226‑4000 | | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Papaya Salad” (no fish sauce, uses lime & chili) | > **Note:** > *All five restaurants are located on the same block (1220‑1120 W 31st St). They share a similar menu layout and many of the vegetarian dishes are listed under “Vegetarian” or “No Egg/No Fish Sauce” options. If you’re looking for a quick, reliable vegetarian Thai meal, any of these will serve you well.* ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai 1. **Ask for “No Egg” and “No Fish Sauce”** – Many Thai dishes contain egg or fish sauce; specifying these will make the dish vegetarian. 2. **Choose “Tofu” or “Vegetable” versions** – Most restaurants label tofu-based curries or stir‑fries as vegetarian. 3. **Check the “Vegetarian” section** – Some menus have a dedicated vegetarian section with dishes like Pad Thai, Green Curry, and Tom Yum Soup. 4. **Request a “Vegetarian” version of a dish** – Even if a dish isn’t labeled vegetarian, the chef can often remove non‑vegetarian ingredients. Enjoy your Thai meal! If you’d like directions, reservations, or more detailed menu info, let me know.
